purpose: Global defensive map connecting network-level censorship, shutdown, allowlisting, DPI, lawful-interception lineage, cross-border telecom dependencies, and foreign-information-manipulation response structures without conflating functional similarity with common command.
epistemic_law: SAME_FUNCTION != SAME_VENDOR != SAME_LINEAGE != SAME_OPERATOR != SAME_CONTROL_PLANE. Attribution requires direct bridge evidence.

ooni.scope: global censorship telemetry from more than 200 countries; OONI Explorer currently exposes measurements across 245 countries and more than 31,000 networks

International connectivity is centralized or separable from a domestic/national service environment.

examples: Citizen Lab 2026 SS7/Diameter surveillance mapped to operator infrastructure in Israel, UK and Channel Islands

priority_watch_clusters.reason: Broad anomaly discovery; promote only after reproducible technical evidence.

anti_overclaim_firewall: A shutdown outside Russia is not evidence of Russian involvement.
A DPI fingerprint similar to TSPU is not a TSPU attribution without device/operator/control-plane linkage.
Russian-origin SORM equipment is not evidence of Russian remote command.
Shared vendor use across countries is not evidence of synchronized policy.
Temporal coincidence alone has zero attribution weight.
Information-manipulation activity and network censorship may coexist without being operationally coupled.
Platform coordination evidence cannot be promoted into telecom attribution without an independent technical bridge.
